updates.finding: Two separate commercial-vessel incidents were reported at Hormuz on Sep. 21. UKMTO reporting carried by AP said an inbound tanker was struck by an unknown projectile; two crew sustained minor injuries, the vessel remained under its own power, and no environmental impact was reported. Later reporting citing UKMTO described an outbound LPG tanker struck by debris from unknown projectiles; crew were reported safe and the vessel continued. Attribution is unresolved and neither incident is assigned to Iran, the United States, or another actor absent further evidence.
updates.drawer_effect: Append both incidents to the Hormuz maritime-threat chronology as separate events; do not merge with earlier Trend or other vessel attacks and do not infer perpetrator.

updates.finding: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK accepted a formal Saudi request for military support and will provide defensive air-to-air refuelling for a limited period. One RAF Voyager is to deploy in the coming days. This converts prior allied-support discussion into a confirmed UK commitment, but does not establish British participation in offensive targeting or strikes.
updates.drawer_effect: Update Saudi external-support drawer: UK request accepted and asset commitment announced. Keep separate from U.S. refusal/non-commitment and French readiness statements.

updates.finding: Reuters reports the United States has rebuffed repeated Saudi requests for direct military support against the Houthis. Separately, Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi requested U.S. support in a Sep. 20 call; two Reuters sources said Trump made no direct pledge of military support. These are distinct dispositions: Saudi requests were rebuffed; the Yemeni request received no direct pledge in the reported call. Reuters could not independently verify the New York Times report that U.S. Houthi strikes were prepared and cancelled at the last minute.
updates.status: SAUDI REBUFF SUPPORTED; YEMEN REQUEST/NO-DIRECT-PLEDGE SUPPORTED; ALLEGED STRIKE CANCELLATION ATTRIBUTED/UNVERIFIED BY REUTERS
updates.drawer_effect: Clarify language in existing drawer: do not describe Yemen as explicitly refused; record no direct pledge. Saudi request is separately reported as rebuffed.

updates.finding: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said foreign airports, fuel suppliers, landing-service providers and ticket sellers serving sanctioned Iranian airlines risk exclusion from the dollar system and predicted Iranian airlines would be shut out internationally from Sep. 23. This is an enforcement threat/prediction, not proof that every Iranian carrier will cease worldwide operations. Iraq was reported preparing to suspend Iranian-carrier flights from Sep. 22; Georgian service by affected Iranian carriers was reported stopped from Sep. 21. Turkish Airlines separately told Iran International it had no Iran flights scheduled before March 2027; that is a foreign-carrier suspension, not direct proof of U.S. sanctions enforcement against Iranian carriers.
updates.status: U.S. ENFORCEMENT POSTURE CONFIRMED; GLOBAL SHUTDOWN OUTCOME NOT YET ESTABLISHED; PARTIAL THIRD-COUNTRY IMPLEMENTATION REPORTED
updates.drawer_effect: Update Sep. 8 aviation-sanctions drawer with announced enforcement mechanism and first reported foreign implementation; verify actual Sep. 23 operating status in subsequent sweep.

updates.finding: G7 foreign ministers meeting on the UN General Assembly sidelines called on Iran to end arming and support of the Houthis, condemned continuing Houthi strikes in Yemen and against Saudi Arabia, and called for an end to military actions, threats and attacks on civilian shipping and a return to the political process. This records the G7 position; it is not independent event-level proof for any particular weapons transfer or attack attribution.
updates.status: CONFIRMED MULTILATERAL POSITION; NOT EVENT-LEVEL ATTRIBUTION PROOF
updates.drawer_effect: Append to diplomacy and Iran-Houthi support-policy drawers while preserving evidentiary distinction between government attribution and independently demonstrated transfer chains.

updates.finding: AP reporting supplies more precise UN-linked figures for the Yemen escalation: 674 deaths, nearly 3,000 injuries and 129,438 displaced. These refine the noon Reuters shorthand of nearly 700 killed, thousands injured and nearly 130,000 internally displaced; the noon observation remains preserved rather than rewritten.
updates.drawer_effect: Use precise denominator for current human-impact status while retaining the earlier Reuters publication state and observation time.

updates.finding: Iran's Revolutionary Guard warned that renewed U.S. escalation would bring changes in Iranian weapons, tactics and targets and separately said forces were ready for a prolonged conflict. The statements establish Iranian military signaling, not demonstrated possession/use of any unspecified new weapon or proof of advance intelligence about U.S. attack plans.
updates.status: OFFICIAL IRANIAN WARNING CONFIRMED; CAPABILITY IMPLICATIONS UNADJUDICATED
updates.drawer_effect: Append rhetoric/signaling node; do not upgrade earlier Iranian foreknowledge or unspecified-new-weapons claims.
